author: Ambika Prasad Singh, Regional Archaeological Officer, Gorakhpur, U.P. State Archaeology Department
asr_identification: mound called Bhuiladih, about 6 km N of Babhanan railway station, Basti district (U.P.): no identification argued
evidence: Surface exploration only: sherds of red ware of the Maurya, Sunga, Kushan, Gupta and medieval periods. No structures, Buddhist finds or inscriptions reported.
quote: A mound known as Bhuiladih, was … explored about Six Km to the north of … Babhanan Railway Station, in district of … Basti. The pot-sherds collected from the … mound mainly are of red ware belonging to … Maurya, Sunga, Kusana, Gupta and
note: The report never names Kapilavastu or Carlleyle. By name and position (Basti district, NW of Basti town) this is presumably Carlleyle's Bhuila Dih, his Kapilavastu (ASR XII, asr_batch4 333-339), long abandoned. The sherds show an Early Historic to medieval settlement mound, nothing more: no support for Carlleyle and no bearing on the study's open choice between Piprahwa-Ganwaria and Tilaurakot (Mizutani 06.02: Tilaurakot). Part of section 36, 'Explorations in district Gorakhpur'; the passage opens with Ahichchhatra plates.
Conservation (Odisha temples; votive stupas and Monastery 1 at Ratnagiri, Jajpur); no identification.

author: B. R. Mani with Sanjay Kumar Manjul and others, Excavation Branch-III, Patna, ASI
asr_identification: Lathiya mound (25°23′37″ N, 83°34′53″ E), 2.5 km SE of Zamania, about 20 km SE of Ghazipur (U.P.), S bank of the Ganges: a Gupta temple site; no Xiyu ji place named
evidence: Excavation of the 158 x 61 m mound beside the standing stone pillar (bell capital with eight lions, once crowned by two back-to-back Garuda figures on a lotus seat). Period I Sunga-Kushan, Period II Gupta in three phases: four brick temples (sanctum and mandapa) of Gupta phases I-II around the pillar, inside an enclosure wall; the pillar's base braced by a brick enclosure; stucco; a dump of hundreds of offering bowls; houses. Antiquities (p. 134) include a copper ring-seal and terracotta sealings in Gupta Brahmi (legends not given). Heavy brick robbing.
quote: The Excavation Branch-III, Patna of … the Survey under direction of B. R. Mani, … about 20km south-east of Ghazipur and … A stone pillar is standing on the … western end of the mound. The top of the … eight broken lions facing eight directions; … member of two Garuda figures back to back … Remains of four brick temples of Gupta
note: No mention of Xuanzang, Garjapatipura or a capital. A Gupta Vaishnava pillar-and-temple complex in the Ghazipur region (07.02), of the sort Xuanzang counts as deva temples (天祠) there, but some 20 km SE of Ghazipur on the S bank: it supports neither Mizutani's Ghazipur (agreed; study: Ghazipur or Sayyidpur, open) nor Oldham's Sayyidpur for the capital. Continued in 794-797.
Continuation of 793 (Lathiya): plans and plates, enclosure walls and Temples 3-4; no place named.
Continuation of 793 (Lathiya): Temple 4, the brick enclosure round the pillar base, Period I walls; no place named.
Continuation of 793 (Lathiya): residential areas, the offering-bowl dump, drains; no place named.

Opening of the BHU Nalanda survey (G. K. Lama): over 100 villages, table of distances from the ruins incl. a 'Xuan-Zang Memorial Hall'; already coded at 785 (iar_batch11), which starts earlier (line 191). The passage then runs into Lauriya Areraj plates (784).

author: Gautam Kumar Lama, Department of Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology, Banaras Hindu University
asr_identification: Kool, 3 km SE of the Nalanda ruins = Kolita, Maudgalyayana's village; Nanan, 7 km SE of the ruins = Nalakagama, Sariputra's birthplace; a natural grotto named Indra-Shila in the Parvati hill SW of Parvati village, 34 km SE of the ruins (Nalanda-Nawada border)
evidence: Surface survey only. Kool: mound 115 x 65 m, 3 m high, Red Ware, sculpture fragments under worship (p. 19). Nanan: mound of 5 acres, 1.5 m high, in the village, Red and Black Ware, sculpture fragments at the Goraiya Sthan and Shiva temple, medieval remains; its printed coordinates repeat Chandi Mau's (p. 20). Parvati: Buddha in dharmacakra-mudra at the Baba Sthan, Red Ware and Kushan brickbats on the hill, a modern Ram-Sita temple (p. 20). Also Chandi Mau, excavated 2000-01, 'a single culture site of Pala period' (p. 15).
quote: Moggallana, one of the chief disciples of … Buddha belong the village named Kolita and … perhaps Kool is its corrupt form. The site … name Nanan may be identified with ancient … Nalakagama, where Sariputra was born and … hill known as Parvati having a natural grotto … named Indra-Shila is located to south-west
note: Codes only what 785 (iar_batch11, same survey) lacks: 785 has Ayer = Buddhavana (09.02.01) and the Indrasila cave at Giriyak (09.03.11), whose entries (pp. 13, 15) also fall in this passage. Kool = Kolita (09.03.08; Mizutani: no identification): a name likeness, attributed to 'scholars of Buddhism', and Kool lies SE of the ruins where Xuanzang has SW. Nanan = Nalakagama (09.03.10; Mizutani: = Faxian's Nala, no site): name likeness, no excavation; Chandi Mau, Broadley's candidate, is Pala only. Parvati grotto: a local name, undated; bears on 09.03.11 (Giriyek, Mizutani agreed) only as the alternative Parbati and agrees with Parbati for Kapotaka (09.03.13, the survey's final view; Mizutani: Bihar). None of these entries names Xuanzang. Bhadari (p. 15, 'Bhadraarya') and Machhaldiha (p. 19, 'Machhalgama') are not Xiyu ji places.

author: Gautam Kumar Lama, Department of Ancient Indian History, Culture and Archaeology, Banaras Hindu University
asr_identification: no identification argued: inscribed images at Silao, 8 km SE of the Nalanda ruins, and at Tetrawan (25°6' N, 85°36' E), 16 km E of the ruins
evidence: Silao: mound 50 x 30 m, 7 m high, Red and Red Slipped Ware; at the Mahadeva Sthan N of the village Buddhist and Brahmanical sculptures, some inscribed, among them an inscribed broken image of Mahakashyapa. Tetrawan: at the Bhagvati temple S of the village a huge black basalt Buddha in bhumisparsha-mudra worshipped as Bhairava Baba, with inscriptions on the lotus petals and the broken halo, undeciphered. The survey concludes that Nalanda's settlement history goes back at least 600 years further.
quote: inscribed broken sculpture of Buddha’s … chief disciple-Mahakashyap … may be made of a huge image of Buddha in … Bhumisparsha mudra made of black basalt … misinterpreted as Bhairava Baba (Pl. 11) … There is a inscriptions on the lotus-petals … and on broken halo of the image which are
note: Silao: Chhabra (EI 25, epig) edited a Pala pedestal of Kasyapa owned at Silao naming his nirvana hill Gurupada (09.01.03, Kukkutapada; study: Gurpa, Mizutani: hill N of Kurkihar); this inscribed Mahakashyapa image may be the same piece or a companion; the IAR does not read it, and it says nothing of where the hill is. Tetrawan: Cunningham's Tetrawa, Xuanzang's monastery 40 li SE of the isolated hill on the Bihar base (09.03.15, unidentified; Cunningham ASR XI read pedestals naming Tentadi-grama there); a further inscribed image, unread, does not decide between Tetrawa and Aphsar. No mention of Xuanzang in these entries.
